claims.claim: Open-label placebo research has reported benefits for chronic low back pain.
claims.finding_supported: In a 2016 randomized controlled trial, adding open-label placebo pills to treatment as usual for three weeks was associated with greater reductions in self-reported pain and back-related disability than treatment as usual alone.

specifics.design: Randomized controlled trial; open-label placebo plus treatment as usual versus treatment as usual.
specifics.population: 97 adults with persistent low back pain lasting more than three months were randomized; 83 completed the trial.
specifics.pain_result: Composite 0–10 pain-score reduction was 1.5 points (95% CI 1.0–2.0) with open-label placebo versus 0.2 points (95% CI −0.3–0.8) with treatment as usual.
specifics.disability_result: Roland–Morris disability-score improvement was 2.9 points (95% CI 1.7–4.0) with open-label placebo versus 0.0 points (95% CI −1.1–1.2) with treatment as usual.

claims.single_correction_to_make_aggressive_cop: Say: "A small 2016 randomized trial reported that open-label placebo pills, added to usual care for three weeks, improved self-reported pain and disability more than usual care alone in chronic low back pain." Do not say it proved that placebo pills treat chronic low back pain generally.

citations.author: Cláudia Carvalho, Joaquim Machado Caetano, Lidia Cunha, Paula Rebouta, Ted J. Kaptchuk, and Irving Kirsch
citations.title: Open-label placebo treatment in chronic low back pain: a randomized controlled trial
citations.finding_actually_supported: Reports the trial design, randomized sample, three-week duration, and between-group changes in self-reported pain and disability.

claims.claim: Open-label placebo studies investigate whether deceptive concealment is necessary for placebo-associated benefits.
claims.finding_supported: Open-label placebo trials transparently tell recipients they are receiving a placebo and test whether outcomes differ from no treatment, waiting-list, usual-care, or other comparator conditions.
claims.single_correction_to_make_aggressive_cop: Say: "Open-label placebo research tests whether some placebo-associated benefits can occur without hiding that the treatment is a placebo." Avoid saying deception has been shown to be unnecessary in every condition or for every outcome.

citations.author: C. Thomaier and colleagues
citations.title: Effects of open-label placebos across populations and outcomes: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
citations.finding_actually_supported: Defines eligible open-label placebo trials as those in which recipients were fully informed they were receiving a placebo and compares them with control conditions.

citations.author: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Program in Placebo Studies
citations.title: Program in Placebo Studies
citations.finding_actually_supported: Describes research on treatment ritual, context, patient-provider relationships, imagination, hope, and expectation as elements of placebo research.

claims.claim: Placebo-related responses may involve real physiologic changes rather than purely conscious belief.
claims.finding_supported: In experimental pain settings, placebo analgesia given with an expectation of pain relief has been associated with measurable changes in endogenous μ-opioid neurotransmission and, in a separate study, changes in an inflammatory cytokine during pain.
material_limits: The strongest evidence concerns experimentally induced pain and placebo analgesic expectation; it does not establish one universal placebo mechanism.
These studies do not show that explicit belief is irrelevant. Their interventions explicitly used analgesic expectations or contextual instructions.
A physiologic correlate does not prove that every reported symptom improvement is caused by the same biological pathway.
claims.single_correction_to_make_aggressive_cop: Say: "Placebo analgesia is not necessarily imaginary: controlled pain experiments have linked analgesic expectations to measurable opioid-system activity and other biological changes." Do not say "belief does not matter" or "placebos work independently of psychology."

citations.author: Jon-Kar Zubieta and colleagues
citations.title: Placebo Effects Mediated by Endogenous Opioid Activity on μ-Opioid Receptors
citations.finding_actually_supported: Using PET during sustained experimental pain, the study found placebo-associated activation of μ-opioid neurotransmission in several brain regions; the intervention involved an expectation of analgesia.

citations.author: Christian S. Pecina and colleagues
citations.title: Effects of placebo administration on immune mechanisms and relationships with central endogenous opioid neurotransmission
citations.finding_actually_supported: In 37 healthy volunteers undergoing a pain challenge, placebo administered under analgesic expectation was associated with lower plasma IL-18 and relationships to endogenous opioid activity.

claims.claim: Ted Kaptchuk is associated with the Program in Placebo Studies and the Therapeutic Encounter at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School.
claims.finding_supported: BIDMC currently identifies the Harvard-wide Program in Placebo Studies and the Therapeutic Encounter, hosted at BIDMC, and lists Ted Kaptchuk as its director.
claims.single_correction_to_make_aggressive_cop: Use the current institutional formulation: "Ted Kaptchuk directs the Harvard-wide Program in Placebo Studies and the Therapeutic Encounter, hosted at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center."

citations.author: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center
citations.title: Program in Placebo Studies
citations.finding_actually_supported: States that the Harvard-wide Program in Placebo Studies and the Therapeutic Encounter is hosted at BIDMC and identifies Ted Kaptchuk as director.

claims.claim: Copables mails inert pills to customers.
claims.finding_supported: Copables' public pages describe a 14-day program that includes a physical placebo product, described on its IBS page as a daily 'OLP gummy,' plus app-guided ritual, cognitive-behavioral exercises, handwritten cards, and AI feedback.
what_is_not_established: The reviewed pages do not establish the fulfillment method, so 'mails' is not verified.

The reviewed pages market the product as a placebo and say 'no chemicals,' but an ingredient list or product specification was not retrieved; pharmacological inertness should not be asserted without that documentation.
The company’s wellness-program claims are company statements, not independent evidence that its bundled protocol reproduces results from any particular clinical study.
claims.single_correction_to_make_aggressive_cop: Say: "Copables markets a 14-day self-guided protocol that includes a physical placebo gummy and digital behavioral exercises."

citations.author: Copables
citations.title: 14-day IBS protocol
citations.finding_actually_supported: Describes daily consumption of an open-label placebo gummy, a guided ritual in an app, digital behavioral exercises, and written field notes.

citations.author: Copables
citations.title: The Science
citations.finding_actually_supported: States that its protocol includes a placebo and a daily handwritten card; it also makes company-level claims about who responds to open-label placebo protocols.

claims.claim: A digital intervention might reproduce some therapeutic ritual or expectancy effect without mailing a physical pill.
claims.finding_supported: A randomized smartphone study in healthy participants showed that a deliberately designed digital placebo intervention could manipulate reported treatment credibility and efficacy expectancy over 20 days. It did not establish that a phone-only ritual produces outcomes equivalent to physical open-label placebo pills, nor did it test chronic low back pain.
claims.single_correction_to_make_aggressive_cop: Say: "A phone-delivered ritual can be designed to shape treatment expectations; whether it can replace a physical placebo for clinical outcomes remains unproven."

citations.author: M. M. F. M. Reiner and colleagues
citations.title: Induction of Efficacy Expectancies in an Ambulatory Smartphone-Based Digital Placebo Mental Health Intervention: Randomized Controlled Trial
citations.finding_actually_supported: In 132 healthy participants, a 20-day smartphone intervention using a mock sound or image tested whether prospective and retrospective messaging could induce efficacy expectancies; expectancy and credibility, not clinical disease outcomes, were the stated endpoints.

claims.claim: Conscious belief is unnecessary for open-label placebo effects.
claims.finding_supported: Open-label placebo trials show that full concealment is not always required. They do not demonstrate that all expectancy, perceived credibility, learning, conditioning, engagement, or treatment context is unnecessary.
claims.why_the_claim_fails: The smartphone expectancy study explicitly manipulated expectancy. Copables itself frames plausibility, active engagement, and adherence as relevant. Meta-analytic evidence also indicates that suggestive instructions can influence open-label placebo effects in some settings.
claims.single_correction_to_make_aggressive_cop: Say: "Explicit certainty that a placebo will work may not be required, but context, expectations, learning, credibility, and engagement may still matter."

citations.author: M. M. F. M. Reiner and colleagues
citations.title: Induction of Efficacy Expectancies in an Ambulatory Smartphone-Based Digital Placebo Mental Health Intervention: Randomized Controlled Trial
citations.finding_actually_supported: Tests induction of prospective and retrospective efficacy expectancies as possible components of a digital placebo intervention.

citations.author: P. Spille and colleagues
citations.title: Open-label placebos—a systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental studies with non-clinical samples
citations.finding_actually_supported: Reports that instruction suggestiveness influenced efficacy for objective outcomes, while rating overall evidence quality low to very low.

strongest_evidence.evidence: The Carvalho trial is the strongest direct support for the chronic-low-back-pain statement because it is the named primary randomized trial and reports its numerical outcomes.

source.author: Cláudia Carvalho and colleagues
source.finding_actually_supported: Open-label placebo plus usual care outperformed usual care alone on self-reported pain and disability over three weeks.

strongest_evidence.evidence: PET evidence is stronger than a general assertion about 'mind over matter' because it identifies a measurable opioid-system correlate under placebo analgesic expectation.

source.author: Jon-Kar Zubieta and colleagues
source.finding_actually_supported: Placebo analgesic expectation was associated with μ-opioid neurotransmission changes during experimentally induced pain.

strongest_evidence.evidence: The current BIDMC program page is the appropriate primary institutional source.

source.author: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center
source.finding_actually_supported: PiPS is Harvard-wide, hosted at BIDMC, and directed by Ted Kaptchuk.

counterevidence.counterfinding: The favorable CLBP result was from a short, unblinded study with self-reported outcomes and a usual-care comparator. It is evidence of a reported result, not conclusive evidence of a broadly deployable treatment effect.

source.author: T. von Wernsdorff and colleagues
source.finding_actually_supported: The review found a positive pooled OLP-versus-no-additional-treatment estimate but emphasized small samples, short durations, heterogeneity, and risk-of-bias concerns.

counterevidence.counterfinding: The broader OLP literature is not uniformly low-risk: an updated review rated only 3% of included primary trials low risk of bias; 77% had some concerns and 20% were high risk.

source.author: C. Thomaier and colleagues
source.finding_actually_supported: Most included OLP trials relied on self-report outcomes potentially affected by participants’ awareness of assignment.

counterevidence.counterfinding: The identified smartphone 'digital placebo' study tested expectancy trajectories in healthy participants, not equivalence to a physical placebo, not a clinical chronic-pain endpoint, and not a head-to-head comparison against a pill ritual.

source.author: M. M. F. M. Reiner and colleagues
source.finding_actually_supported: The intervention’s central measured outcomes were credibility and efficacy expectancy.

counterevidence.counterfinding: Available mechanistic evidence often invokes expectation, instructional framing, conditioning, and treatment context. That is inconsistent with treating the absence of explicit belief as evidence that psychological processes do not matter.

source.author: Jon-Kar Zubieta and colleagues
source.finding_actually_supported: The placebo intervention examined was administered with an expectation of analgesia.

open_questions.question: Did the Carvalho chronic-low-back-pain result replicate in adequately powered, longer-term trials using comparators that control for attention, ritual, and demand characteristics?
Which components of an OLP protocol matter independently: the pill or gummy, explanatory rationale, clinician contact, adherence, behavioral exercise, conditioning, or positive suggestion?
Can a phone-only intervention produce clinical outcomes comparable with a physical OLP protocol for a specified condition?
What are the exact ingredients, dose form, price, fulfillment method, and return/shipping terms for Copables products?
Has Copables itself published or preregistered independent outcome data for its complete commercial protocol, rather than citing component studies conducted elsewhere?

sources_to_verify.why: Needed before saying the company mails products or that its product is pharmacologically inert.
sources_to_verify.preferred_source: Current official product label, ingredient panel, checkout/shipping policy, and terms of sale.

sources_to_verify.why: No price was established from the reviewed public pages.
sources_to_verify.preferred_source: Current official checkout page or pricing page.

sources_to_verify.why: The identified digital placebo study supports expectancy manipulation, not equivalence between a phone intervention and a physical OLP product.
sources_to_verify.preferred_source: A preregistered randomized head-to-head trial in the target condition comparing phone-only, physical OLP, combined protocol, and credible attention control.

sources_to_verify.why: This formulation conflates explicit belief with expectancy, rationale credibility, conditioning, treatment ritual, and engagement.
sources_to_verify.preferred_source: Primary factorial trials that separately manipulate explicit expectancy, conditioning, ritual, and disclosure.
